security.title: Payment confirmation has no replay guard
security.why: The handler does not check whether the order is already paid before calling PayPal. The classic API hides this because it returns the same transaction, but the modern API will refuse a repeat capture, so behaviour changes.
security.fix: Check the stored order status first; make the confirmation idempotent on the server.

security.title: Order listing is public
security.why: Returns every order (tokens, amounts, buyer emails, transaction ids) without authentication; the tokens also unlock the refund endpoint.
security.fix: Remove it or require admin authentication.

security.title: Refund endpoint has no authentication
security.why: Anyone who can reach this URL and knows (or guesses) an order token can trigger a refund of real money.
security.fix: Require an authenticated admin session and CSRF protection; log every refund.
security.evidence: RefundTransaction behind an open HTTP endpoint

security.title: Credential with a hardcoded fallback value
security.why: Secrets live in source code (a fallback is still a committed secret and masks a missing environment variable).
security.fix: Read credentials only from the environment or a secret store; fail loudly when missing. The REST migration replaces user/password/signature with OAuth2 client id and secret.

security.title: IPN handler accepts a verified message without checking it matches an order
security.why: After PayPal says VERIFIED it still does not check: receiver_email, amount/currency comparison, duplicate txn_id check. A genuine notification for a different payment could mark an order paid.
security.fix: Check receiver, amount, currency and transaction id against the stored order and ignore duplicates. In the migration: verify the webhook signature and match the event to an order.

<?php
require_once __DIR__ . '/../config.php';

// Classic PayPal NVP (name-value pair) API client.
function paypal_nvp($method, array $params = []) {
    $post = array_merge([
        'USER'      => PAYPAL_API_USERNAME,
        'PWD'       => PAYPAL_API_PASSWORD,
        'SIGNATURE' => PAYPAL_API_SIGNATURE,
        'VERSION'   => PAYPAL_NVP_VERSION,
        'METHOD'    => $method,
    ], $params);

    $ch = curl_init(PAYPAL_NVP_ENDPOINT);
    curl_setopt($ch, CURLOPT_POST, true);
    curl_setopt($ch, CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS, http_build_query($post));
    curl_setopt($ch, CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER, true);
    curl_setopt($ch, CURLOPT_TIMEOUT, 30);
    $raw = curl_exec($ch);
    curl_close($ch);

    parse_str((string)$raw, $out);
    return $out;   // e.g. ['ACK' => 'Success', 'TOKEN' => 'EC-...']
}

function paypal_ok($r) {
    return isset($r['ACK']) && ($r['ACK'] === 'Success' || $r['ACK'] === 'SuccessWithWarning');
}
